svg.title: Resolve Identity Before Asserting Entitlement
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-resolve-identity-before-entitlement; chapter number: 5; title: Resolve Identity Before Asserting Entitlement; subtitle: Separate candidates, test evidence, document uncertainty, and verify the economic premise.; caption: Christa Cowen on Ancestry separates namesakes; FamilySearch presenters distinguish negative evidence and require written conflict analysis; Katherine Moore separates genetic leads from confirmation; Heir Hunters illustrates unknown estate value.; assumptions note: Christa Cowen, FamilySearch presenters, Katherine Moore, and Heir Hunters supply distinct checks. Genetic confirmation applies when genetic evidence is used; no DNA threshold automatically establishes identity or inheritance.; note: Katherine Moore's 228 cM match advanced an identification investigation but did not replace further testing and investigation. Heir Hunters' 53-heir Wearing case did not establish the estate's value.; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: Have competing namesakes been separated through relatives, places, chronology, and associated records?; pass next: G2; fail action: Keep candidates separate and compare original images. Cowen's five Daniel Joneses could not be distinguished by their shared farming occupation.; gate: G2; question: Does each claimed absence concern information expected in an extant source rather than only a failed search?; pass next: G3; fail action: Record the unsuccessful search without treating it as proof of absence, following the FamilySearch distinction.; gate: G3; question: Are conflicts written up and relevant genetic-tree connections documented, with leads distinguished from confirmatory identification?; pass next: G4; fail action: Preserve provisional relationships, explain unresolved conflicts, and obtain the further testing or investigation Katherine Moore requires when applicable.; gate: G4; question: Has estate value been established separately from the number of heirs?; pass next: Evaluate the documented case without equating heir count with recovery value.; fail action: Keep the value unconfirmed. Heir Hunters' Wearing investigation and Katherine O'Connell's mineral-rights case show why family size is not an earnings estimate.

circle.title: gate: G1; question: Have competing namesakes been separated through relatives, places, chronology, and associated records?; pass next: G2; fail action: Keep candidates separate and compare original images. Cowen's five Daniel Joneses could not be distinguished by their shared farming occupation.

gate: G2; question: Does each claimed absence concern information expected in an extant source rather than only a failed search?; pass next: G3; fail action: Record the unsuccessful search without treating it as proof of absence, following the FamilySearch distinction.

gate: G3; question: Are conflicts written up and relevant genetic-tree connections documented, with leads distinguished from confirmatory identification?; pass next: G4; fail action: Preserve provisional relationships, explain unresolved conflicts, and obtain the further testing or investigation Katherine Moore requires when applicable.

gate: G4; question: Has estate value been established separately from the number of heirs?; pass next: Evaluate the documented case without equating heir count with recovery value.; fail action: Keep the value unconfirmed. Heir Hunters' Wearing investigation and Katherine O'Connell's mineral-rights case show why family size is not an earnings estimate.
